fields.Name: Sales: Product Mix and Discount Depth
fields.UserQuestion: What products are we selling, how often do they attach to a deal, and how deep are the discounts?
fields.Description: Product mix, attach rate and discount depth at the LINE grain (master plan §9.1, §9.3 measure 11). REBASED FROM DealLine ONTO OrderLine: the embedded-order rework retired DealLine, so lines now live on the order a deal carries. Same grain, same catalog dimension, same measures — only the source table moved, and it moved closer to the catalog, since OrderLine.ProductID is NOT NULL with a real FK.
fields.TechnicalDescription: Grain: OrderLine, joined via Deal.OrderID. Every money column is READ AS STORED — UnitPrice, DiscountPct, DiscountAmount, LineTotalNet were written by the orders engine and nothing here recomputes them; AvgDiscountPct is a statistic about stored percentages. Attach rate uses DISTINCT deals as its numerator and denominator, because a product on three lines of one deal has not attached three times. Both discount forms are reported, since a mix of percent- and amount-based discounts makes either alone misleading. Date: the DEAL's actual close, falling back to expected.

_comments: PARAMETERS ARE DERIVED BY MJ, NOT DECLARED HERE -- and the authored detail is kept below.
They were declared as relatedEntities['MJ: Query Parameters'], and that made this whole
directory unseedable on a fresh database. MJ derives parameters from the SQL when the query is
created; the declared rows then collided with them on the UNIQUE (QueryID, Name) index -- 18
violations, whole-transaction rollback, 0 of 16 queries landing, byte-identical on a retry.
That was KI-25, and it cost every fresh install its dashboard.
Removing the declarations lets MJ derive them: names and IsRequired come out identical. Type
degrades from date to string on the period parameters, which is harmless here because
QueryForecastSource passes them as ISO date-only STRINGS on purpose -- 'a full timestamp would
invite a query to compare a date column against an instant'. What would genuinely have been
lost is the authored Description and SampleValue, so they are preserved verbatim:
CompanyID (string)
Selling company. Omit for every company. Deal.CompanyID is server-stamped from the pipeline, so it is always present and never needs a fallback.
PipelineID (string)
One pipeline. Omit for all pipelines.
PeriodStart (date)
Inclusive start of the window. Omit for no lower bound.
PeriodEnd (date)
Inclusive end of the window. Omit for no upper bound.
WonOnly (string)
Pass "true" to count only won deals — what was actually sold rather than what is being offered.
e.g. true
